scenes.title: Hook: Which Hill Is Steeper?
scenes.say: Imagine two ramps. One climbs gently, the other shoots up steeply. How could we measure exactly how steep a line is? Let's find out.
scenes.visual: A coordinate grid with x and y axes labeled. Two straight line segments drawn as ramps: one shallow in blue, one steep in orange. Small arrows pulse along each line.

scenes.title: Pick Two Points
scenes.say: Start with any line on a grid. Choose two points that sit exactly on it. Here we have point A at x equals one, y equals two, and point B at x equals five, y equals six.
scenes.visual: A straight line crosses the grid. Points A at (1, 2) and B at (5, 6) appear as glowing dots with coordinate labels fading in beside them.

scenes.title: Draw the Rise and the Run
scenes.say: Now build a right triangle. Move straight up from point A until you line up with point B. That vertical distance is the rise. Then move straight across to point B. That horizontal distance is the run.
scenes.visual: From A, a vertical green segment draws upward to y equals six and is labeled rise. A horizontal red segment draws from there to B and is labeled run. The triangle fills in lightly.

scenes.title: Count the Rise and Run
scenes.say: The rise goes from two to six, so it is four. The run goes from one to five, so it is also four. Count the units to check.
scenes.visual: Tick marks appear along the vertical and horizontal segments. Equations write out on screen: rise equals six minus two equals four, and run equals five minus one equals four.

scenes.title: Slope Equals Rise Over Run
scenes.say: Slope is rise over run. Four over four equals one. So this line has a slope of one. It rises one unit for every unit it runs.
scenes.visual: The equation slope equals rise over run appears in large text. Then 4 over 4 equals 1 is written, with the fraction bar animating. The line is highlighted and labeled slope equals 1.

scenes.title: Practice Question
scenes.say: Try this one yourself. A line passes through the points at x equals two, y equals three, and x equals six, y equals eleven. What is its slope? Pause the video, work it out, then check your answer.
scenes.visual: A new grid shows the two points (2, 3) and (6, 11) with a blank triangle. Text reads: Find the slope. Rise equals ? Run equals ? Slope equals ? A pause icon appears.
